explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/417: with V'(x) = #{φ(m) : 1 ≤ m ≤ x} and V(x) = #{φ(m) ≤ x : m ≥ 1}, does lim V(x)/V'(x) exist? The Lean statement asserts a limit L exists in ENNReal for the real-parameter ratio as x → ∞; using ENNReal allows L = ∞, which is appropriate since the page notes Erdős suggested the limit may be infinite. Numerator is #{k ∈ range φ : k ≤ x}, which includes φ(0) = 0 in Mathlib, so it equals V(x)+1 for x ≥ 0; since V(x) → ∞ this shift does not affect the existence or value of the limit. Denominator is exactly V'(x). Faithful (yes/no question stated in its positive form).
